# Python-ASIC-Flowscope

**Python-ASIC-Flowscope** is a Python automation library for parsing, extracting, and analyzing the logs, reports, and gate-level netlists generated by **OpenROAD** and **OpenLane** ASIC backend (RTL-to-GDSII) flows.

It was built to remove the manual, error-prone process of opening dozens of individual report and log files after every physical design run. Instead, each stage of the flow — synthesis, floorplanning, placement, clock tree synthesis (CTS), routing, and sign-off — is automatically summarized into a single, clean, human-readable report, using Python's `re` (regular expressions) library to extract the key metrics.

The library is designed to be **generic and reusable**: every script takes the relevant directory (reports, logs, or netlist path) as a command-line argument, rather than hard-coding paths, so it can be dropped into any OpenLane/OpenROAD design without modification.

---

## Features

- ✅ Automated **stage-by-stage report summarization** (synthesis, floorplan, placement, CTS, routing, sign-off)
- ✅ Automated **log parsing** for warnings, errors, and stage completion tracking
- ✅ **Liberty (`.lib`) file parsing** utilities, including NAND2 area extraction for area normalization (K-NAND2 units)
- ✅ **Gate-level netlist parsing** for I/O extraction
- ✅ Direct integration into OpenLane's `flow.tcl`, so reports/logs are generated automatically at the end of each run — no manual invocation required
- ✅ Consolidated, readable `.txt` summary reports for quick inspection or downstream comparison scripts

## How It Works

### 1. Report Parsing (`reports/`)

Each OpenLane stage produces multiple raw report files (timing, power, area, slew, skew, DRC/XOR results, etc.). A dedicated script per stage (`test_syn.py`, `test_floorplan.py`, `test_placement.py`, `test_cts.py`, `test_routing.py`, `test_signoff.py`) parses these files using regular expressions and extracts the key metrics, including:

- Design area (µm²) and normalized area (K-NAND2 units, via `nand_area.py`)
- Worst Negative Slack (WNS) / Total Negative Slack (TNS)
- Worst setup and hold slack
- Clock skew (pre/post CTS)
- Power (total, per corner)
- Slew and fanout violation counts
- DRC/XOR violation counts
- Wire length and via counts per metal layer (routing stage)

`run_all_reports.py` acts as the top-level orchestrator, calling every stage script in sequence and writing each summary to `reports/` (or the equivalent `outputs/reports/` directory in this example run).

### 2. Log Parsing (`logs/`)

Parses the raw OpenLane/OpenROAD `.log` files per stage, extracting warnings, errors, and flow progress markers to make debugging failed or flagged runs faster — without needing to scroll through the full flow log manually.

### 3. Liberty & Netlist Utilities

- `nand_area.py` extracts the NAND2 gate area from the design's liberty (`.lib`) file, used to normalize design area into K-NAND2 units for technology-independent area comparison.
- `in_out/` contains the gate-level netlist parser, used to extract primary input/output ports directly from the post-synthesis or post-routing netlist.

### 4. OpenLane Flow Integration (`modified_flow.tcl`)

`modified_flow.tcl` is a modified version of OpenLane's native `flow.tcl`, with two additional procedures:

```tcl
proc run_all_reports_step {args} {
    puts_info "Running report summary scripts..."
    set reports_path $::env(REPORTS_DIR)
    set result [exec python3 reports/run_all_reports.py $reports_path]
    puts_info "$result"
}

proc run_all_logs_step {args} {
    puts_info "Running log parsing scripts..."
    set logs_path $::env(RUN_DIR)/logs
    set result [exec python3 log/run_all_log_parsers.py $logs_path]
    puts_info "$result"
}
```

These are hooked into the main flow sequence right after `generate_final_summary_report`, so that report and log summaries are generated **automatically** at the end of every OpenLane run, with zero manual intervention.

Similar summaries are generated for the floorplan, placement, CTS, routing, and sign-off stages, and saved into `outputs/reports/`.

---

## Usage

### Run report summarization manually

```bash
python3 reports/run_all_reports.py <path_to_reports_dir>
```

### Run log parsing manually

```bash
python3 logs/run_all_log_parsers.py <path_to_logs_dir>
```

### Automatic integration with OpenLane

Replace (or merge) your OpenLane `flow.tcl` with `modified_flow.tcl`, so that `run_all_reports_step` and `run_all_logs_step` are invoked automatically at the end of every flow run.

---

## Requirements

- Python 3.8+
- Standard library only (`re`, `os`, `sys`, `datetime`) — no external dependencies required
- Designed for use alongside [OpenLane](https://github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenLane) / [OpenROAD](https://github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD)

---

## Motivation

This project was developed as part of the ICpedia Internship Program (Physical Design / PnR Team) to support large-scale design space exploration — sweeping clock periods, utilization, and placement/CTS parameters across many OpenLane runs. Manually inspecting reports and logs for each trial was not scalable; this library made it possible to automatically trace, compare, and validate metrics (area, timing, power, DRC) across every run.
